title: A nonlinear exercise diastolic-pressure threshold does not establish added cross-hospital CAD prediction
abstract: We tested whether excess peak-minus-rest diastolic blood pressure above15mmHg improves angiographic CAD prediction beyond flexible additive clinical/exercise measures. Hungarian development included293 patients; frozen Swiss institutional validation included120,112 disease-positive. Brier loss changed from0.240983 to0.244934;baseline-minus-augmented improvement-0.003951,1000 joint source-refit/target-bootstrap95% interval[-0.023110,0.016746]. Source CV worsened. Linear-baseline sensitivity improved Brier whereas nonlinear,penalty,and omitted-incompatible-field challenges did not establish benefit. Extreme case mix,unavailable Swiss cholesterol and protocol mismatch limit inference. Zero-coded missing values were corrected;invalid-run summary retained. This is not proof of absent DBP physiology or clinical utility. AI-authored,self-checked,clean offline rerun supplied.
